ca/quebec.title: Flag of Quebec (Fleurdelisé)

colors.note: Represents the French heritage of Quebec.
The fleurs-de-lis and the cross, symbols of Catholic and French tradition.

desc:
- The Fleurdelisé (1948) features a white cross on blue with four white fleurs-de-lis. It represents Quebec's French heritage and Catholic roots
- **Construction:** a blue field with a white cross dividing four white fleurs-de-lis
- Each fleur-de-lis is centred in its quadrant, pointing toward the centre
trivia:
- The fleurdelisé was adopted in 1948, making it older than Canada's maple leaf flag (1965)
- The four white fleurs-de-lis represent the French colonization and Catholic heritage
- Quebec's flag is one of the most recognizable provincial flags in North America

ca/ontario.title: Flag of Ontario

colors.note: Red ensign tradition from the British heritage.

desc: - The Ontario flag is a Red Ensign bearing the provincial shield: a red cross of St George over three gold maple leaves on green
- **Construction:** a Red Ensign with the Union Flag in the canton and the Ontario shield (red St George's Cross above three golden maple leaves on green) in the fly
trivia:
- The Union Jack reflects Ontario's position as Canada's most populous province
- The shield represents Ontario's coat of arms
- Ontario was originally Upper Canada during British colonial rule

ca/british-columbia.title: Flag of British Columbia

colors.note: The Pacific Ocean that borders the province.
The wavy stripes representing the Pacific waves.

desc:
- The flag of British Columbia features a Union Jack in the upper portion with a crown at the centre, above a setting sun over blue and white wavy stripes representing the Pacific Ocean
- Adopted on 20 June 1960, it is the only Canadian provincial flag that incorporates the full Union Jack
- The design was adapted from the provincial coat of arms granted by King Edward VII in 1906
- **Construction:** the Union Jack (defaced with a crown) occupies the upper half
- The lower half has a golden half-sun above alternating blue and white wavy horizontal stripes
- Ratio approximately 3:5
trivia:
- The setting sun represents the province's western location
- The wavy blue and white lines represent the Pacific Ocean
- British Columbia is Canada's westernmost province

ca/alberta.title: Flag of Alberta

colors.note: Blue ensign background representing loyalty to the Crown.

desc: - A deep blue field bearing the shield from the provincial arms: a St George's Cross over wheat fields, prairies, foothills, and Rocky Mountains
- **Construction:** an ultramarine blue field bearing the shield from the coat of arms of Alberta (mountains, foothills, prairie, wheat) centred
trivia:
- The prairie and mountains represent Alberta's diverse landscapes
- The colours represent energy and enthusiasm
- Alberta is known for the Rocky Mountains and oil resources
